# 1 Clement Chapter 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 16

**16:1** For Christ belongs to the humble-minded, not to those who exalt themselves over his flock.

**16:2** The scepter of the majesty of God — the Lord Jesus Christ — did not come with a display of boasting or arrogance, though he was able to do so, but in humility of mind, as the Holy Spirit spoke concerning him.

**16:3** For it says: "Lord, who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? We proclaimed before him as a young child, as a root in parched ground; he has no form or glory; and we saw him, and he had no form or beauty; but his form was without honor, less than that of men, a man in affliction, who knows how to endure sickness — because his face was turned away from us; he was dishonored and not counted." [Isa 53:1-3 LXX]

**16:4** "He bears our sins and is pained for our sakes; and we accounted him to be in toil and affliction and ill-treatment." [Isa 53:4 LXX]

**16:5** "But he was wounded on account of our transgressions and was bruised for our iniquities. The chastisement of our peace fell upon him; by his bruises we were healed." [Isa 53:5 LXX]

**16:6** "All we like sheep went astray; every one strayed from his own way; and the Lord gave him over for our sins." [Isa 53:6 LXX]

**16:7** "And he, because he was ill-treated, opened not his mouth. As a sheep he was led to the slaughter; and as a lamb before its shearer is silent, so he opened not his mouth." [Isa 53:7 LXX]

**16:8** "In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. Who shall declare his generation? For his life is taken up from the earth." [Isa 53:8 LXX]

**16:9** "Because of the transgressions of my people he was led to death." [Isa 53:8b LXX]

**16:10** "And I will give the wicked in exchange for his burial, and the rich in exchange for his death; because he practiced no iniquity, nor was any deceit found in his mouth." [Isa 53:9 LXX]

**16:11** "And the Lord wills to cleanse him from his wound. If you offer for sin, your soul shall see a long-lived offspring." [Isa 53:10 LXX]

**16:12** "He shall see light and be satisfied; and with his knowledge my righteous servant shall justify many, and he shall bear their sins." [Isa 53:11 LXX]

**16:13** "Therefore he shall inherit many, and he shall divide the spoils of the mighty, because his soul was given up to death, and he was counted among the transgressors; and he bore the sins of many, and on account of their sins he was given up." [Isa 53:12 LXX]

**16:14** And again he himself says: "But I am a worm and no man, a reproach of men and despised by the people. All who saw me mocked me; they spoke with their lips and shook their heads, saying, 'He trusted in the Lord; let him rescue him; let him save him, since he takes pleasure in him.'" [Ps 22:6-8 LXX]

**16:15** You see, beloved, what the example is that has been set before us; for if the Lord was thus humble-minded, what should we do, we who through him have come under the yoke of his grace?

---

*LOGOS formal equivalence. Isaiah 53 and Psalm 22 are both cited as Christ-hymns of humility.*
